subject: Proposal: retroactive pin for 2026-era quantized variants
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Sarah K. <sarah@acme.chat>
Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Proposal: retroactive pin for 2026-era quantized variants

Hi team,

TL;DR: I propose we do a targeted, retroactive pin of a subset of 2026-era quantized variants for customers still on older tokenizers to avoid a spike in inference errors when we flip the default routing in July. This would be a short-lived pin (30–45 days) tied to a migration cadence and telemetry gates.

Why now: we saw two customer-facing incidents in April/May where tokenization differences between the 2026 quantized builds and newer tokenizer runtime produced malformed outputs (truncated code blocks, escaped JSON blobs). The incidents affected non-negligible production traffic for one long-tail customer (Acme ChatOps) and a handful of internal QA flows.

Proposal overview:
- Pin the following variants (subset in attached compat matrix) for customers who: tokenized_histogram shows > 2% mismatch and are on legacy tokenizer v1.7.
- Pin window: 2027-06-01 -> 2027-07-16 (45 days).
- Telemetry gates: tokenization-mismatch-rate < 0.1% for two consecutive days to begin staged ramp to new default.
- Migration steps: run a sweep to identify eligible customers, notify them with migration guidance, and schedule automated fallback lifts once gates met.

Requests for each of you:
- Priyom: can you validate the list of variants in the compat matrix and confirm there are no runtime ABI constraints for rolling a pin at the variant level? Also include perf delta expectations for the quantized builds we propose to pin.
- Marissa: ops ask—if we pin, what changes in routing and capacity planning? Will this create hot spots on any Dedicated pools?
- Lauren: product ask—do we need to route the pin as a temporary feature-flag-based policy (so customer can opt-out) or as an automatic fallback? Also need phrasing for customer comms.

Attachments: compat-matrix-202605-202612.xlsx, tokenizer-diff.patch, retro-pin-migration-plan.md

I put Sarah (Acme) on the thread because her team hit the issue and she'd appreciate visibility. Please reply with snags or a 1–3 line ack if you can take the action. I can run the customer sweep script on Monday if we align.

Thanks,
Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior PM, Model Ops
Redwood Inference
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 10:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposal: retroactive pin for 2026-era quantized variants

Thanks for the clear proposal—+1 on a short-lived pin. A few technical datapoints and open questions from my side: 

1) Variant list check: I scanned the matrix. The core issue stems from a token-to-byte offset shift introduced in tokenizer v2.0 that some older quantized exporters implicitly depended on. The variants you flagged (Q-202606A, Q-202611X-lite) are safe to pin; they carry the older tokenizer expectations baked into their byte-packing layer.
2) Runtime constraints: pinning is straightforward from the runtime side—routing can target model:variant pins. The caveat is pinned variants still share KV-cache encoding differences. If a customer mixes pinned and unpinned variants in the same session, KV mismatch could cause context corruption. We should strongly recommend single-variant sessions during the pin window.
3) Perf delta: expected token throughput drop for the pinned quantized builds is ~5–8% vs the latest fast-path builds. I added perf numbers as comments in compat-matrix.

Action items I can take this week:
- Run a dry-run compatibility sweep across the customers flagged in the matrix (will produce a per-customer risk score) by Monday EOD.
- Produce a short runbook note on how to detect KV-corruption symptoms in telemetry and automatic mitigation hooks (I’ll attach).

Question for Marcus/Marissa: do we need automated routing policies that detect KV-corruption signals and immediately flip the customer to a fallback variant, or do we keep that manual for this short window? Automated flips can be risky but reduce mean time to mitigation.

– Priyom
Senior SW Eng, Inference Compatibility
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Sarah K. <sarah@acme.chat>
Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposal: retroactive pin for 2026-era quantized variants

Appreciate the heads-up. Operational notes:

- Capacity: pinning those variants will create localized load on nodes that host the older quantized runtime. We have capacity buffers but need to pre-warm Dedicated pools for customers with > 10 RPS sustained traffic to avoid queueing. I'll coordinate with infra to spin up pre-warmed hosts on 2027-05-30 if we get final variant list today.
- Routing: we can implement a short-lived routing rule by customer ID that maps to variant pin; SDK/API changes are minimal. The route applier accepts a start/stop timestamp so cleanup is trivial.
- Hotspots: Acme is flagged as medium-risk because of their high burstiness in sync jobs. Recommend we onboard them to a canary lane with throttled burst capacity and a documented rollback path.

Regarding automation on KV-corruption signal: for safety, keep flips manual for the first 72 hours post-rollout, then consider enabling automated revert if signal clearly exceeds threshold. Ops will provide a one-pager for rollback steps.

I’ll own the capacity plan and will follow up with exact host counts and costs by EOD.

Marissa
Head of Dedicated Ops
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Cc: Sarah K. <sarah@acme.chat>
Date: Sat, 29 May 2027 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposal: retroactive pin for 2026-era quantized variants

Thanks all—this reads reasonable. A few product/comms points: 

- Customer-facing wording: we should present this as a "compatibility stabilization" step and be explicit about the temporary nature and the migration assistance we will provide. Draft blurb: "We’re temporarily pinning a model variant to preserve expected outputs while we migrate tokenizer implementations — your workload will be unaffected, and our team will coordinate the flip once validation gates are met."
- Opt-out: make the pin opt-out for customers who explicitly want the latest build (developers experimenting), but default to pinned for the risk cohort. Include opt-out request flow (support ticket + two-business-day acknowledgement).
- Timeline: from a roadmap perspective, I need assurance we won’t extend beyond 45 days without exec approval. Please capture extension criteria in the migration plan (we require exec sign-off if metrics don’t converge by day 30).

Priyom/Marissa, please loop in the CS lead for Acme (Sarah is cc’d) to coordinate a short sync next week. Marcus—if you can convert the migration plan into a one-page timeline with gates (I’ve annotated the MD), I’ll review and prepare the customer note.

—Lauren
Director, Product Management
